newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA sees delay on Airbus A3XX airliner.
newsitem.headline: DASA sees delay on Airbus A3XX airliner.

text.p: Partners in the Airbus consortium, who on Monday agreed to turn the plane maker into a joint-stock company by 1999, have delayed a decision on building a large airliner, the chairman of Germany's DASA said.
Manfred Bischoff told the Stern magazine that no decision was expected this year on the A3XX project -- a high-capacity plane intended to compete with Boeing's 747 Jumbo Jet.
"Talks with airlines showed that there is still a need for in-depth consultation over big aeroplanes," Bischoff said in an interview released ahead of the magazine's publication.
"This project requires an enormous financial effort and must be examined from all angles before we begin."
He added that new companies would be founded to build the A3XX project and a planned 100-seater aircraft. Airbus would have a controlling stake in both, with the remainder taken up by other partners.
Airbus groups French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, DASA -- a unit of Daimler-Benz AG -- and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA).
Bischoff said it might be possible to bring the "first class" aerospace sector of the former Soviet Union into such projects.

He said that Airbus would seek new partners in future, and also ultimately carry out a stock market flotation -- echoing a view expressed on Monday by BAe. "But I don't see that in the next few years," Bischoff added.

The goal of the new Airbus company must be to achieve a return on equity of at least 12 percent for its shareholders, Bischoff said. That meant that Aerospatiale must match cost cuts of 30 percent already made by DASA and BAe, he said.

Bischoff also called for Airbus to move away from a principle of unanimity to decision-making by majority. He said he expected the first chief executive of the new Airbus company to be French, with the supervisory board chairman a German.
